title: Practice 2.1
role: Team member talking with a colleague about a change at work and how it feels
can_do: I can talk about a change at work and how I feel about it.
I can weigh advantages and disadvantages with on the one hand and on the other hand.

items.prompt: Which sentence compares two sides of a situation?

options.text: On the one hand it saves money; on the other hand, it costs jobs.

items.explanation: On the one hand ... on the other hand ... presents two sides.

o1.text: This states a fact but gives no contrast.

o3.text: This is a simple past sentence.

items.template: {1} the plan is risky, it could improve our results.

error_tag.text: Although introduces a contrast; because gives a reason.

items.explanation: Although links two ideas that seem to oppose each other.

items.template: I feel {1} about the new role: I am worried but hopeful.

error_tag.text: Choose a word for a mixed or worried feeling.

items.explanation: Uncertain, mixed, uneasy, anxious and nervous all fit.
Although introduces the first clause; the main clause follows.

error_tag.text: Although + clause, then the main clause.

items.prompt: Match the feeling with its meaning.

right.text: unable to cope with too much
happy that a worry has ended

items.explanation: Each word describes a different feeling at work.

items.prompt: Say how you feel about a change. Use I feel.
accepted: I feel anxious about the change
I feel nervous about the change
I feel relieved about the change
I feel excited about the change
items.explanation: I feel + adjective + about + the change.
